column3: The immediately preceding warning identifies Satan as disobedient to the Merciful, directly grounding the feared Satanic allegiance.
A messenger warns his people against false worship because he fears a painful day of punishment for them.
Contrasts the focus's feared allegiance to Satan with the secure state of God's true allies.
Links wrongdoing to becoming people of the Fire, a consequence parallel to the focus's warning.

Declares God alone as wali and helper, directly opposing Satan as wali.

Satan promises support before battle and then disowns his followers, showing the unreliability of his claimed alliance.
Believing men and women are awliya of one another in a life of right action, a communal positive counterpart.

Satan disavows those who followed him and says he only called them, directly exposing the end of the feared relation.

The command to worship God supplies the immediate positive alternative to worshipping Satan.
Those who take awliya besides God are answered by divine judgment, providing a direct false-allegiance counterpart.

Devils are assigned as companions to those who reject guidance, a parallel to becoming attached to Satan.
God alone is wali and gives life to the dead, directly opposing all substitute protectors.
Devils bar their companions from the path while those companions suppose themselves guided.
Wrongdoers are awliya of one another, whereas God is wali of the God-fearing.
